title: An agent can report its sub-agents to decade
body:
An agent reports to decade with `agent` messages on the socket (`AgentUpdate` in `decade-channel/src/lib.rs`, the `Agents` section of `docs/protocol.md`). The report carries one state for the whole agent (attention, done, working or idle), an activity line, a question, the model, context, tokens and cost. Nothing in it describes sub-agents or background tasks the agent has started. When the agent's turn ends while sub-agents still run, the agent reports `done`, and the workspace card turns green while work is still going on.

The fix for the wrong state belongs in coax first: it should keep reporting `working` while background work runs. This issue is the protocol side, so decade can show that work.

## Proposal

- `AgentUpdate` gains `subagents`: the list of sub-agents and background tasks the agent is running, each with a name, a one-line activity and a state (working, done or failed). An agent sends the whole list each time it changes. An empty list or an absent field means none.
- The workspace card's state line shows the count, such as `coax working · 2 sub-agents`, and the hover popover lists each sub-agent with its activity.
- A workspace whose agent reports `done` while a sub-agent still works sorts and colours as `working`.
- The `agents` MCP reply includes each agent's sub-agents.

## Cost

`AgentUpdate` is public in `decade-channel`, so the field moves its minor version. The protocol change moves `decade`'s minor. coax needs to send the list.

## Open

- Whether a finished or failed sub-agent stays in the list until the agent's next turn, or leaves as soon as it ends.
- Whether nested sub-agents are reported, or only the agent's direct ones.
- Whether a failed sub-agent should raise the workspace to `attention`.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/5da9dd6b
notes.text: Decided with Jack. decade shows the sub-agent list as the agent last sent it; when finished entries leave is the agent's call. Only direct sub-agents are reported; deeper work can go in a sub-agent's activity line. A failed sub-agent does not raise the workspace to attention; the popover shows it with a red mark, and the parent agent reports attention itself if it needs the person. coax sending the list is coax's own work, filed in coax's foam.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/5da9dd6b
notes.text:
Stopped before writing code. The card has no room for the count as the proposal words it, and how it should read there is a question about looks.

The card's state line is `state_text` in `decade/src/chrome/frame.rs`. It reads "coax working · 4m", with " +N" after it when the workspace has other agents. `fit` cuts anything past the line's room and ends it with an ellipsis. The room is 28 columns at the 8 by 18 cell the frame tests use. The popover's state lines have 32 columns.

| line | columns |
|---|---|
| `coax working · 4m` | 17 |
| `coax working · 4m · 2 sub-agents` | 32 |
| `coax working · 4m · 2 sub-agents +1` | 35 |
| `claude needs you · 12m · 2 sub-agents` | 37 |

So the common case is cut on the card to "coax working · 4m · 2 sub-ag…". In the popover, the same line is 34 columns with its glyph, two past the room.

Options for the card:

- Drop the age while sub-agents run, as the proposal's example does: "coax working · 2 sub-agents" is 27 columns. A longer agent name or "needs you" still overflows.
- A short form after the age, such as "coax working · 4m · 2 sub" (25 columns) or a glyph and a number.
- Put the count on the card's fourth line, before the activity, or on the usage line.

I lean to the first, since it matches the proposal's example. I left the choice to Jack. Two smaller questions about the popover need the same answer. One is whether its state lines carry the count, given that the popover lists the sub-agents under them. The other is how many lines each sub-agent takes. The popover moves up to stay inside the window, and a long list can still run past the window's bottom.

The rest of the issue does not depend on this choice. It covers the `subagents` field, the effective `working` state, and the `agents` MCP reply.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/5da9dd6b
notes.text: Jack chose: the card's state line stays as it is, and the count goes at the start of the card's message line, as in '2 sub-agents · reading the tests'. The popover's state line carries no count; each sub-agent takes one line (state mark, name, activity cut to fit), and after five a last line says '+N more'. An agent update without the subagents field keeps the last list, like every other agent field; [] or null clears it.
